kicker: Vehicle makers · sales growth vs margin change, Q2 FY27
title: Vehicle sales jumped; margins fell at 11 of 13
dek: Makers of cars, bikes, trucks and tractors grew Q2 sales a median 25%, but steel, copper and rubber rose faster than prices. Maruti rose 3.11% on 20 Nov after a record October for the industry, yet its Q2 margin fell 3.1 points.

stats.note: Steel +17% and rubber +40%, per M&M's Q2 call. Escorts Kubota faced 8–9% cost inflation against 3.5% in price hikes.

stats.note: About 400 basis points year on year, while its discounts fell to 2.9% of price from 3.2%.

read: Demand was not the constraint; margins now depend on how much of the metal-price rise makers can pass on before Q3's further cost increases land.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Maruti move: HDFC Sky, 20 Nov 2026; October sales: Business Today, 13 Nov 2026
notes: Sales growth and EBITDA margin (operating EBITDA over revenue from operations) are from filed Q2 FY27 and Q2 FY26 results as computed by Vantage, except Bajaj Auto, TVS Motor and Ashok Leyland, where standalone figures stated on their Q2 calls are used because the consolidated figures include a newly consolidated KTM (Bajaj) or a lending arm (TVS Credit, Hinduja Leyland Finance); on consolidated filings TVS's margin fell 1.1 points. The 13 are listed makers of cars, two- and three-wheelers, trucks, buses and tractors worth ₹1,000 crore or more; Ather (no year-ago base), Keto Motors (no base), Olectra (filed and call margins disagree), dealers and construction-equipment makers are left out, and M&M's consolidated figure includes Mahindra Finance. Causes are from Q2 FY27 calls: commodity inflation (M&M: steel +17%, copper +42%, rubber +40%; Hero: material costs up about 5.5% over two quarters, about half recovered in price), while discounts were not the cause at Hyundai; Hero also carried a ₹168 crore loss on its VIDA electric scooters. Bajaj held its margin with price rises, a weaker rupee (₹95.5 a dollar realised vs ₹87.1) and incentives under the government's production-linked (PLI) scheme. News hook: Maruti rose 3.11% on 20 Nov 2026, among the top Nifty gainers (HDFC Sky), after the industry's record October sales, with passenger vehicles above 5 lakh (Business Today, 13 Nov 2026); Maruti has no Q2 call in our data and Eicher's Q2 entry covers Q1, so no cause is stated for them.
